name: Mintlify
tagline: Hosted developer documentation from MDX files in your repo, with search, API reference and AI answers.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Mintlify is a very well designed wrapper around a solved problem: turn MDX files into a docs site. A coding agent can scaffold an Astro or Next docs site with sidebar nav, dark mode, code tabs, client side search and an OpenAPI-driven reference page in a single sitting, and static hosting is free. What you are actually paying Mintlify for is that you never touch any of it, plus the AI chat over your docs, hosted preview deploys per pull request and a web editor your non-technical teammates can use. For one person documenting one project, none of that is load bearing. For a team shipping a public API where docs are a sales surface, the polish and the zero-maintenance part start to look cheap.
coreLoopDIY: Renders a folder of MDX files into a fast static docs site with sidebar navigation, full-text search, syntax-highlighted code blocks with copy buttons, and an API reference page generated from an OpenAPI spec.
requirements: a git repo and any static host (GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify)
an OpenAPI 3 spec if you want the API reference page
optional: an LLM API key if you bolt on docs chat later
whatYouLose: AI chat and semantic search over your docs, which is the one piece that is genuinely annoying to rebuild well
Per-pull-request preview deploys and a hosted CI pipeline you never think about
A web editor and visual diffing for teammates who will not open a code editor
Design taste by default: your DIY theme will look fine, not obviously expensive
Built-in docs analytics, search-term reports and broken link scanning
moatNotes: The moat is aesthetic and operational, not structural. Nobody is locked in by their MDX files, which is exactly why Mintlify competes on looking better than Docusaurus.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because docs are a public artifact and taste is expensive. Companies pay so that their reference site looks credible on day one, so that every branch gets a preview URL, and so that nobody on the team owns a build pipeline that breaks the week before launch. The AI answers layer is the other real reason: it is the difference between docs people search and docs people ask, and rebuilding that with embeddings, chunking and a decent citation UI is its own project.
notes: Static site generators have been eating this lunch for a decade; Mintlify just plated it better.
prompt:
Build a static developer documentation site generator in an empty folder. No accounts, no telemetry, no backend.

Stack, non-negotiable: Astro 5 with @astrojs/mdx, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Shiki for syntax highlighting, Pagefind for search. Output is a fully static site in dist/.

Content model:
- Docs live in src/content/docs/**/*.mdx with frontmatter: title, description, order, group.
- Validate frontmatter with an Astro content collection schema and fail the build on missing title.
- Sidebar navigation is generated from folder structure plus the group and order fields, no hand-maintained nav file.

UI requirements:
- Three column layout: left sidebar nav, center prose, right on-page table of contents built from h2 and h3.
- Dark mode via a class on html, toggle button, remembered in localStorage, no flash on load.
- Code blocks with a language label, a copy button, and a Tabs component for multi-language examples.
- Callout components: Note, Warning, Tip. Card and CardGroup components for landing pages.
- Keyboard shortcut Cmd+K opens a search modal backed by Pagefind, arrow keys and Enter navigate.
- Prev and next page links at the bottom of every page.

API reference:
- Read an OpenAPI 3 spec from openapi.yaml at the repo root at build time.
- Generate one page per operation: method, path, description, parameters table, request body schema, response schemas, and a copyable curl example.
- If openapi.yaml is absent, skip this cleanly instead of erroring.

Also include:
- A build-time internal link checker that fails the build on broken relative links.
- npm scripts: dev, build (runs Pagefind index after astro build), preview, check-links.
- Seed content: a quickstart page, two guide pages, and an index page using Cards.
- A GitHub Actions workflow that builds and deploys to GitHub Pages on push to main.

Out of scope, do not build: AI chat over docs, analytics, auth, versioned docs, i18n, comments.
Any future API keys go in .env with a .env.example committed. Write a README explaining how to add a page and how to swap the OpenAPI spec.
